Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 3/10, warning but contained vs VIX Spike Tier 2/4, skew active AND backwardation active simultaneously
Price has not broken down, so the crash index stays at 3. But the options market is already paying for near-term protection via both skew (elevated put demand) and backwardation (near-dated vol priced above long-dated vol). VIX structure signals lead price; trust the options read over the crash index here.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score 47/100, ACCUMULATE partial signal vs Regime bias, RISK-OFF with 3 aligned signals
A partial accumulation signal and a 3-signal risk-off regime pull in opposite directions for anyone making a sizing decision. The partial contrarian print reflects deteriorating sentiment, not a confirmed low. At three aligned signals, the risk-off regime is the higher-confidence read.
Today's tension
Prices hold but the structure underneath is cracking: VIX options signal a vol expansion that the crash index has not yet confirmed.
Bull
The crash index sits at only **3/10**, well below extreme readings that precede disorderly moves. The contrarian score at **47/100** is generating a partial accumulation signal, meaning sentiment has weakened enough for a counter-trend entry.
Bear
VIX backwardation and skew are both active, meaning options traders are paying up for near-term protection right now. **69.8%** of tracked cross-asset pairs are diverging, with **26** bearish pairs versus only **4** bullish ones out of **43**, and the regime carries a three-signal risk-off bias.
The tell: Whether QQQ and SPY re-correlate: that pair has drifted from **+0.83** to **-0.29**, and a re-tightening above zero would signal the broad market is healing.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime is in TRANSITION at 54/100, biased risk-off with three aligned signals. The CONCENTRATION macro regime at 55% confidence tells you this is a market where a narrow set of positions is doing the heavy lifting. The advance is thin and the bench is short. Crowded trades unwind fast when few positions are driving returns.

The partial contrarian read at 47/100 is real but incomplete. You need it to push above the full-signal threshold before adding exposure. Right now it is telling you sentiment is deteriorating, not that the low is in. The crash index at 3/10 says no systemic pressure yet, but the VIX structure signals (skew and backwardation both active) say the options market is already leaning against that calm. Sit lighter than normal on gross exposure.

The read that flips this stance is a crash index dropping back toward zero with the VIX term structure returning to contango. Until those two re-align, the risk-off bias is the anchor. Three signals do not get overridden by one partial contrarian print.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence, in plain terms, means that assets which normally move together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift means the historical relationship between two assets has shifted, sometimes reversing sign entirely.

Right now 69.8% of the 43 tracked pairs are diverging, with 26 carrying a bearish tilt against only 4 bullish ones. The composite sits in a TOPPING zone with the mother jaws score at a perfect 100.

The most dramatic breaks are QQQ versus SPY (drifted from +0.83 to -0.29), meaning tech and the broad market are no longer moving as one unit, and value versus momentum (drifted from +0.72 to -0.71), a near-complete reversal of their relationship. NVDA versus AMD has flipped from -0.78 to +0.38, meaning these two semiconductors now move together after spending an extended period moving against each other.

Regional banks (KRE) have decoupled from broad financials (XLF), drifting from +0.19 to -0.68. When this many pairs break at once inside a TOPPING zone, the signal is late-stage distribution, not constructive consolidation.

Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The Nikkei leads Asia at +3.1% over five days while Shanghai is down -2.3%, a spread of 5.4 percentage points within the same region, signaling these two markets are pricing very different stories. Europe is uniformly soft: the SMI is best in class at -0.1% and the DAX trails at -0.8%.

In the US, the Dow is down -1.0% while the Russell 2000 is down -2.8%, confirming that small-cap stress is the sharper end of domestic selling. In crypto, Solana at +1.7% is holding while Bitcoin is down -0.9%, a divergence between the two that typically appears when risk-seeking capital rotates into higher-beta positions even as the broader session softens.

Across all four regions, the consistent signal is that large-cap and defensive assets are outperforming, and the Russell at -2.8% is the clearest domestic confirmation of the risk-off regime.

Forward-looking indicators · Bonferroni-validated
Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The crash index at 3/10 says the current environment is in active surveillance but nowhere near historical blow-up readings. That sounds calm.

But both VIX skew and VIX backwardation are lit simultaneously. Backwardation means the market is paying more for near-dated volatility than for longer-dated vol, a structure that appears when traders expect a move soon rather than eventually.

Skew means the bid for downside puts is elevated relative to calls. The crash index measures what has already happened in price; the VIX structure measures where options traders are placing money right now.

These two can coexist: price has not broken, so the crash index stays low, while options market participants are buying protection ahead of a potential acceleration. The calm in spot prices may not persist.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
